prompt: A catalogue claims to contain the Cartesian product of its sizes and colours. A new colour is added, but only one size is offered in that colour. Is the claim still correct?

options.text: Yes, because the new colour appears somewhere.
options.explanation: A product requires every pairing, not just coverage of each separate category.

options.text: No, unless that is the only size: every size must pair with the new colour.
options.explanation: All combinations of the two input sets are required.

options.text: No, because a Cartesian product cannot change.
options.explanation: Products can change when their input sets change.

options.text: Yes, because order never matters in a pair.
options.explanation: A product has fixed roles for first and second coordinates; missing pairs remain missing.

workedExample: Take any other size. The pair consisting of that size and the new colour belongs to the product of the declared domains, but is absent from the catalogue. The catalogue may be a relation selecting allowed pairs; it is no longer the full product.
